title: OpenStax Chemistry 2e, 4.2: Oxidation-Reduction Reactions
kind: Assistant paraphrase of consulted textbook section, not verbatim quotation
notes: Oxidation involves electron loss or increasing oxidation number; reduction involves gain or decreasing oxidation number. The reducing agent is oxidized; the oxidizing agent is reduced. Redox is generally identified through oxidation-number changes, including covalent reactions without literal electron transfer. Elemental atoms have oxidation number zero; monatomic ions have their charge as oxidation number. Oxygen is usually -2, with exceptions. Historically, oxidation referred to oxygen reactions. The section treats complementary oxidation and reduction and gives reaction-classification examples.

title: OpenStax Chemistry, 17.1: Balancing Oxidation-Reduction Reactions
locator: Opening review; half-reaction balancing; Check Your Learning
kind: Assistant paraphrase of consulted textbook section, not verbatim quotation
notes: Redox balancing conserves atoms and charge. Separate half-reactions describe oxidation and reduction; their electron counts must cancel in the combined equation. Electrochemistry links redox chemistry with electricity, including batteries. Copper(II) ions can be reduced to copper metal and thereby act as oxidizing agents.
